hook: The glover's son from Stratford who became the greatest writer in English.

pages.x: William Shakespeare was born in 1564 in Stratford-upon-Avon, the son of a glove-maker, and probably went to the local grammar school. At 18 he married Anne Hathaway, eight years older than him, and they had three children, among them twins.

For seven years he vanishes from the records. Legends say he was caught poaching deer, or held horses outside theatres. By 1592 he was in London as an actor and playwright, and a jealous rival sneered at him as an "upstart crow".

In 1599 his company built the Globe Theatre on the south bank of the Thames. Up to 3,000 people crowded in, the poorest standing in the yard for a penny. In 1613 a cannon fired during a play set the thatched roof alight, and it burned to the ground.
He wrote comedies, histories and tragedies, about 39 plays in all. Romeo and Juliet, about two teenagers from feuding families in Verona, became the most famous love story ever told.
In Hamlet, a prince of Denmark must avenge his murdered father: "To be, or not to be: that is the question." Othello, King Lear and Macbeth followed, the greatest tragedies in English.

More than a thousand words and phrases are first found in his writing: "eyeball", "bedroom", "lonely", "swagger", "break the ice", "wild-goose chase" and "heart of gold" among them. Some he invented; others he was just the first to write down.

He retired to Stratford, a rich man, and died in 1616. In his will he left his wife "my second best bed". In 1623 two friends gathered 36 of his plays in the First Folio; without it, about half of them would be lost.
Shakespeare is the most famous writer in the English language, and his plays are performed more than any other playwright's, in every major language.
pts: Wrote Romeo and Juliet, Hamlet and Macbeth
The greatest writer in the English language
Gave English hundreds of words and phrases
